items.title: List of spellcheck dictionaries (with fix)
items.body:
Hunspell dictionaries have files with underlining: xx_XX
GetLanguage uses names with hyphens: xx-XX

[Before](https://i.imgur.com/uheku0S.png)

The proposed fix may not be perfect but works.
The second condition is for dictionaries such as Polish, which do not have the standard two-letter version (pl), but only the extended one (pl_PL).

items.title: An interesting issue related to the interface language
items.body:
Today during the translation tests, I wanted to do an additional test on a "clean" environment, i.e. without .ini files.
What happened?
On my system (Windows 10 Professional Polish) Sigil with Polish translation started right after the start. I thought "Wow!", but I look at Preferences, and still "English".
Interestingly, until you open "Preferences" and `ui_language` not saved to the file sigil.ini - the Polish (and probably also different) interface starts every time.

Interesting, is not it?

This is not a significant problem, so you don't have to stop preparing for release.

items.title: UX: Default Alt shortcuts interfere with some keyboard layouts
items.body:
## Description

The mainstream keyboard layout in Poland, so-called "Polish Programmer's", relies on combinations Alt/Option+Letter for letters with diacritics. While this is not common in the world in general, a quick Google yields that there seem to be other countries using this layout approach.

Defaults in Sigil override these combinations for its own shortcuts which is really annoying as it makes it impossible to type words in my language. Moreover, some of those combinations can execute potentially destructive actions (see example below), and it is difficult to have to pay attention to something so automatic as typing.

After looking I noticed the possibility to change these in the settings, which is good. However, not after accidentally deleting some words without immediately realising what had happened. (I have decided to write this, as I am currently reading the book and keep finding odd mistakes I just didn't know I introduced!)

## Example

With the "Polish Programmer's" keyboard layout press the combination Alt+a. The action executed is "Search > Replace All". Instead, the expected output is the letter "ą".

## Suggestion

Change the default keyboard shortcut settings (are they widely used?). No other program I have used uses Alt+Letter combination for shortcuts.

(I could submit a PR myself, but I don't want to put in the effort to ruin someone's workflow; equally, I think it's a really annoying little problem.)

items.title: Does SIGIL complies with Antidote SDK's features  ?
items.body:
Hi everybody

I use SIGIL to work on a 500 pages french book, on Windows.
I use "Antidote" software that is a good advanced corrector for french and english (https://www.antidote.info/en/antidote-10)
Antidote have an SDK with a COM API for Windows (https://www.antidote.info/en/antidote-10/documentation/developer-tools)
The Antidote SDK documentation explains :
a) Your application must allow access to text using character positions. Example: Antidote may send a request to your application to return the text between characters 1023 and 1725.
b) Your programming infrastructure (language, libraries, etc.) must allow access Antidote's COM interface.
c) You need to be able to implement a COM interface in your application.
d) Antidote and your application must be running simultaneously. The API simply allows them to communicate with each other.

**So I just need to know if SIGIL complies with this features above** :-)

I've some programming skill (c++, c#, VB.NET, ATMEL µC assembly and c++)

Bests regards
[Antidote-API_COM-v2.0.R2-en.pdf](https://github.com/Sigil-Ebook/Sigil/files/5881500/Antidote-API_COM-v2.0.R2-en.pdf)

items.title: Files starting with #
items.body:
Hi, I was using Sigil 0.9.18 until yesterday, updated to the new version (1.2), and found a bug which makes 1.2 unusable for me.

I checked other versions, this bug exists since 0.9.991.

To check it, create a new and empty epub,
You have by default one text called "Section0001.xhtml"
Add a blank text (=> Section0002.xhtml)
Rename the new text to #Section0002.xhtml
You will notice immediately that this text does not stay at its (second) position but jumps up to the top position.
Save the file, and reopen it.
Sigil will complain that files exists that are not listed in the manifest, and after opening #Section0002.xhtml is gone.

The really bad thing here is that I openend a file that had some text starting with an #, creatd with 0.9.18.
1.20 opened it without problems. All the #-texts showed up. But renaming one of those puts all the #-ones on top, and after a save they were all gone. No warning while  saving the file, only when trying to reopen it (in other words, when it was too late)

I'm back to 0.9.18, which does not have any isses with #-texts, 
Oh, all on Win64.

One more thing, not a bug, but I wondered about this one all the time.
I have stored many own searches.
When I use one of them on a large text with "count all" I usually get pretty quick a result. Assume it does not find anything, then count all tells me "0 results" let's say in half a second. But when I do "replace all" it takes 10 seconds to find out that it does not find anything. Why can't "replace all" be as fast as "count all" when it does not find anything to replace?
